fresh_q_only_baseline.decision: The indirect q-only AA advantage reproduced on five fresh master seeds, although at approximately four rather than seven percentage points.

allele_linked_recruitment.interpretation: Deleting allele-linked recruitment greatly increased both absolute loss and the RR disadvantage. Allele-linked recruitment therefore buffers mismatch rather than generating the AA matching advantage.

local_allele_selection.mediator_note: Deleting local allele selection reduced AA-RR high-trait-mass, allele-frequency and refuge differences to values whose paired CIs included zero at generations 20 and 40, making it the leading single-edge sorting candidate without meeting the predeclared risk-resolution rule.

joint_local_allele_and_trait_selection.interpretation: Local ecological selection as a joint block is required for the late AA matching advantage. The single-edge evidence points toward q-dependent allele sorting, but does not individually resolve it by the predeclared risk criterion.

density_to_q_feedback.interpretation: Removing density from q prevents all functional loss by generation 20 and greatly delays collapse, so N->q feedback enables the deterioration regime. Because the generation-20 endpoint becomes degenerate, this is not treated as clean matching-specific mediation; at generation 40 the differential attenuation is unresolved.

baseline_temporal_signature.interpretation: AA initially concentrates more high-trait mass into fewer occupied patches; by generations 20-40 it retains both the upper-tail mass advantage and more realised refugia. This concentration-to-persistence crossover is a trajectory signature, not by itself a causal certificate.

updated_mechanistic_model.sorting: Local ecological selection as a joint block creates the late matching advantage; secondary mediator evidence points primarily toward q-dependent allele sorting, while the single-edge risk contrast remains unresolved.
updated_mechanistic_model.buffering: Allele-linked recruitment is strongly protective overall and disproportionately buffers the reversed/mismatched state; removing it triples the AA-RR loss contrast.
updated_mechanistic_model.failure_gate: Density-dependent N->q feedback controls whether the forcing trajectory enters early system-wide functional loss, but is not resolved as the unique source of the late AA-RR differential.
updated_mechanistic_model.synthesis: Within the q-only closure, long-horizon relational fate is better described as selection-mediated spatial sorting opposed by recruitment-mediated buffering, under a density-feedback failure gate. This replaces the earlier interpretation that allele-linked recruitment itself generated the matching advantage.

claim_ceiling: These pathway assignments apply to the declared finite q-only closure. Local allele selection is the leading single-edge sorting candidate but remains unresolved by the preregistered risk-DID rule. Do not call density feedback a matching-specific mediator at generation 20 because deletion eliminates all events. Do not generalize sorting, buffering or the observed horizons as universal natural laws.
